title: The Sectors of the Indian Economy: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary

questions.question: Which of the following is correctly classified?
questions.rationale: Banking is a service, hence tertiary. Mining extracts natural products (primary), construction makes structures (secondary), and fishing extracts from nature (primary).

questions.question: Mining and quarrying are conceptually part of the primary sector because they:
options: Merely extract nature's stock without transforming it
Are always run by the government
Employ the largest share of workers
questions.rationale: Extraction without transformation defines the primary sector, even though India's national accounts report mining within the 'industry' block.

questions.question: The Industrial Policy Resolution that reserved the 'commanding heights' of the economy for the public sector was adopted in:
questions.rationale: The IPR of 1956 placed heavy industry, mining, and power in Schedule A (state monopoly), creating PSUs such as SAIL, BHEL, and NTPC; 1991 reversed much of this.

questions.question: India's structural paradox is that agriculture:
options: Produces over half of GVA but employs a tenth of workers
Employs about 45% of workers but produces only about 15-18% of GVA
Employs and earns an identical share
questions.rationale: Roughly half of India's workers earn only about a sixth of output in farming, making productivity per farm worker the lowest of the three sectors.

questions.question: Which sector contributes the largest share of India's gross value added today?
questions.rationale: Services contribute about 53-55% of GVA, far ahead of industry (~28%) and agriculture (~15-18%), making India a services-led economy.

questions.question: A plumber employed by a municipal corporation with a pension and paid leave is best described as:
questions.rationale: Government employer means public sector; registration and service security (pension, leave) mean organised/formal — the two classifications cut across sector of activity.

questions.question: Roughly what share of India's workforce is in the unorganised (informal) sector?
questions.rationale: Around 90% of Indian workers are informal — farm labour, street vendors, home-based workers — lacking written contracts and social security.

questions.question: In 1950-51, the primary sector's share of India's GDP was approximately:
questions.rationale: At Independence agriculture and allied activity produced more than half of GDP; its share has fallen steadily to roughly 15-18% today.

questions.question: 'Premature tertiarisation' refers to India's pattern where:
options: Manufacturing rose to 40% before services dominated
Services became dominant while manufacturing stayed stuck near 15-17% of GDP
Agriculture re-emerged as the largest sector
questions.rationale: Unlike East Asian economies that industrialised massively first, India's services overtook industry early and manufacturing's share has hovered around 15-17% for decades.

questions.question: Under the MSME classification revised in 2020, a 'small' enterprise is one with:
options: Investment up to ₹1 crore and turnover up to ₹5 crore
Investment up to ₹10 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore
Investment up to ₹50 crore and turnover up to ₹250 crore
questions.rationale: Micro: ₹1 cr/₹5 cr; small: ₹10 cr/₹50 cr; medium: ₹50 cr/₹250 cr — the 2020 revision merged earlier manufacturing and services criteria.
